findings.where: The ruled ground of the whole page, at both widths: the feint rules and the double margin line, worst behind the hero and the palette and motion-sketch text
findings.fault: The rules are dark olive and the margin line is dark brown. They read as heavy stripes running behind every line of text, so the ground fights the type. The page also stops looking like a legal pad. A legal pad is known by its pale blue feints and double red margin, and the direction card asks for exactly those. The tile's own texture swatch and palette (Feint #93B3D3 'rules', Margin red 'margin') show them too. So the page says one thing and its swatches say another.
findings.who_objects: Mark asked for a lined yellow legal pad because of his legal background, and this reads more like striped exercise paper. The founder is choosing between five directions, and here the tile's swatches and the page disagree on the one texture this direction stands on. A bank officer reading the standfirst or a post reads through stripes.

findings.where: The motion-sketch timeline table (desktop and phone), and the article title and the script pull quote on phone
findings.fault: The look only works if every text block keeps the 32 px line spacing, and the page breaks that itself. The table's smaller, tighter rows have rules running through the words. On phone the article title's lines straddle the feints, while the pull quote is pulled out to double spacing to stay on them. Ordinary content like a table, a long title or a caption already breaks the pad.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who adds posts and PDFs with no designer (client value 9). Every table, list or long headline she adds will either have rules cutting through it or need hand-tuned spacing. Mark will see his articles looking crossed out.

findings.where: First screen, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.' and the hero copy as a whole
findings.fault: After the heading and standfirst, the first screen's only proof is a size claim, set as its own emphasised line like a tagline. Nothing above the fold says who Mark works for (development banks and agencies) or in which regions. It shows no named body besides the World Bank and no recent work or talk.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer at a development bank judges an advisor by kind of project, region and named bodies. To them 'over 40 years' is an adjective, not evidence, and a featured years line edges toward the boast the brief rules out (client value 6).

findings.where: The end of the page at both widths: no footer, and the 'Write to me' note
findings.fault: The page stops after the motion sketch with no footer, though the palette names Binding for 'nav, footer'. Mark's email address never appears as text. The only contact route is a handwritten 'Write to me' that opens a mail client, and the visitor never sees, and cannot copy, the address.
findings.who_objects: Bank and agency staff who use webmail or a locked-down work machine, where a mailto link opens nothing useful. They want to copy the address into their own client. Anyone who scrolls to the end finds no way to reach Mark and no identity line.

findings.where: Palette, the swatch labels (name, hex, role) in the first row at both widths
findings.fault: Each three-line label ends almost touching the swatch below it. The gap above the next row is no bigger than the gap between a swatch and its own name, so the labels float between two swatches instead of grouping with their own (proximity).
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder reading the tile to judge the palette. They have to work out whether 'rules' or 'ground' belongs to the swatch above or below.
